summary: Validated app-surface record for the Disable Audio Ducking card. The research provider now surfaces the current app action, which writes UserDuckingPreference=3 for the current user.

setting.name: Disable Audio Ducking
setting.casual_explanation: This sets the Windows communications ducking preference so the system does not reduce other audio volumes during calls.
setting.why_people_change_it: People change it when they do not want Windows to lower media volume automatically during communications activity.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The single-value control is straightforward and reversible. Applying it pins the Communications preference to the Do nothing state; rollback should restore the previous value or remove the explicit override.
setting.professional_notes: The research app-surface manifest projects this record through app/Services/TweakProviders/ResearchAppSurfaceTweakProvider.cs. The current engine implementation writes UserDuckingPreference=3 on the current user profile, and the app provider loader de-duplicates the older first-party copy by id after the research provider is loaded.

allowed_values.label: Windows or tool default
allowed_values.meaning: Windows keeps the existing or default communications-ducking preference because the value is not explicitly set.

allowed_values.label: Do nothing
allowed_values.meaning: Sets the communications ducking preference to 3, which corresponds to the Do nothing state used by the current app.

targets.notes: The current engine tweak writes UserDuckingPreference=3 on the current user profile.

app_current_implementation.notes: The research manifest now surfaces this card. The older first-party AudioTweakProvider implementation remains in code, but the live provider loader adds the research provider first and de-duplicates the same tweak id.

writes.notes: The current engine tweak writes UserDuckingPreference=3 on the current user profile.

windows_defaults.label: Hold current or default state
windows_defaults.applies_to: Windows profiles where no explicit communications-ducking override is desired

states.rationale: Leave the communications-ducking value unset unless the user explicitly chooses the Do nothing profile.

windows_defaults.notes: The app rollback path can restore the previous snapshot; the record default story keeps the unset state as the safest generic baseline.

recommended_profiles.label: Windows or existing default
intended_for: Systems where communications ducking should stay at the existing profile
avoid_for: Users who want Windows to stop lowering other audio during calls

states.rationale: Keep the current or default communications-ducking behavior.

recommended_profiles.good_when: You want Windows to keep its existing communications-ducking behavior.
recommended_profiles.bad_when: You want other audio to stay unchanged during calls.
tradeoffs: No explicit user override is written.
Windows or the existing profile can still reduce other audio during communications activity.

recommended_profiles.label: Current app profile
intended_for: Users who do not want Windows to lower other audio during calls
avoid_for: Users who prefer Windows communications ducking

states.rationale: Write the Do nothing communications-ducking preference used by the current app.

recommended_profiles.good_when: You want calls and communications apps to stop reducing media or game audio.
recommended_profiles.bad_when: You rely on automatic ducking to make call audio easier to hear.
tradeoffs: Other audio remains at its normal volume during communications activity.
Call audio may be less prominent in a noisy mix.
recommended_profiles.notes: This is the app-surfaced profile and maps to UserDuckingPreference=3.

validation_proof.exact_quote_or_path: mmsys.cpl Ghidra string/xref probe found UserDuckingPreference in two naturally resolved decompiled functions, including call sites that reference SHGetValueW and SHSetValueW. The paired ETW stackwalk run evidence/raw/etw-stackwalk/peripheral-audio-ducking-etw-20260507/normalized-registry-bundle.json captured an exact RegQueryValue event for UserDuckingPreference during the guest registry probe.
validation_proof.notes: Validated on 2026-05-07 with QGA-first VM tooling. Ghidra provides the code-side mmsys.cpl string/xref evidence; ETW provides a runtime registry trace with caller-stack capture for the exact value name. A stale value left by an earlier Procmon timeout was removed after the evidence run and the guest was verified back to value_exists=false.

evidence.title: QGA ETW stackwalk - UserDuckingPreference runtime registry probe
evidence.summary: The 2026-05-07 QGA-first xperf REGISTRY stackwalk captured a narrow RegQueryValue run for HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Multimedia\Audio\UserDuckingPreference. The normalized bundle is ok, contains 5221 registry events, 1357 caller-stack events, and an exact UserDuckingPreference RegQueryValue event.

evidence.title: QGA Ghidra string/xref - mmsys.cpl UserDuckingPreference handlers
evidence.summary: A headless Ghidra run on C:\Windows\System32\mmsys.cpl found two UserDuckingPreference matches with naturally resolved decompilation output. The markdown export shows SHGetValueW and SHSetValueW call sites for the value name.

decision.why: The value path, app write, runtime trace, static mmsys.cpl string/xref evidence, and rollback story now converge. The research provider can safely surface the current app profile while preserving previous-value rollback.
